smoke.cmd: npm test  (= node --test, per package.json scripts.test)
smoke.notes: Every test spawns a real server process and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio; the test signer is re-derived from DESIGN.md §2, not imported from server.mjs (test/mcp.test.mjs:5-7). Honest harness note: `node --test test/` (trailing dir arg) fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Node v24.21.0 — the working invocation is the package.json script `node --test` (auto-discovery). No network, no API keys used.

essence: Fleet receipt chain as signed append-only MCP organ; fail-closed named errors.

ideas.name: qmr1 receipt dialect
ideas.statement: A receipt is exactly five fields {seq, prev, body, id, sig}; id = SHA-256("qmr1:"+seq+":"+prev+":"+canonicalJSON(body)) is the chain link, sig = HMAC-SHA256(secret, "qmr1:sig:"+id); genesis prev = 64 zeros. Canonical JSON binds the body by canonical form, so key reordering and whitespace never break verification — only value edits do (DESIGN.md §2).

ideas.name: re-derivation over trust
ideas.statement: verify_chain() re-parses the store from disk and re-derives every id and signature from genesis, failing closed on the FIRST broken row with a named, grep-able code at a named at_seq — the fleet's instrument against the 'well-formed, checkable, wrong artifact' finding (DESIGN.md §3, §6).

ideas.name: admission is fail-closed
ideas.statement: append_receipt validates structure → body shape → seq (tip+1) → prev (tip id) → id (recomputed) → sig (HMAC); first failure wins as a tool error carrying the named code; nothing invalid is ever written; there is deliberately no sign_receipt helper — the server stays a verifier, never a co-signer (DESIGN.md §3).

ideas.name: honest MCP wire surface
ideas.statement: Stdio newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 with the MCP handshake (initialize + version negotiation + notifications/initialized), exactly three tools (read_receipts / verify_chain / append_receipt), protocol errors -32601/-32600/-32700, and recall that never lies: reads re-parse from disk each call and surface corrupted_lines instead of silently skipping them (server.mjs:59-73, 222-233).

parts.name: canonicalJSON
parts.essence: Recursive key-sorted, no-whitespace serialization; arrays keep order, object keys sorted lexicographically at every depth — the binding form for everything hash-relevant.
parts.gate: keys sorted at every depth; arrays keep order; output is deterministic across processes

parts.name: receipt id formula (chain link)
parts.essence: id = SHA-256("qmr1:" + seq + ":" + prev + ":" + canonicalJSON(body)) — the body, sequence and parent are all inside one hash.
parts.gate: recomputed id must equal stored id

parts.name: receipt signature formula
parts.essence: sig = HMAC-SHA256(secret, "qmr1:sig:" + id) — symmetric spike scheme; attribution is fleet-trust, stated honestly, Ed25519 per-agent keypairs are the additive qmr2 path (DESIGN.md §4).
parts.gate: recomputed HMAC must equal stored sig

parts.name: genesis rule
parts.essence: GENESIS_PREV = '0'×64; the first receipt has seq 1 and prev = GENESIS_PREV — the chain has exactly one root and every store answers to it.
parts.gate: row 1 prev must equal GENESIS_PREV (enforced via the same prev-linkage check)

parts.name: disk re-parse (no-cache honesty)
parts.essence: loadStore() re-reads and re-parses store.jsonl on every call — every answer describes the file as it IS now, not as it was at boot; unparseable lines are collected, never silently skipped.
parts.gate: no answer is served from a cached view of the file
parts.failure_mode: E_STORE_CORRUPT (named line numbers of non-JSON lines)

parts.name: verifyChain genesis re-derivation
parts.essence: Row-by-row loop from genesis checking, in order: structure → seq → prev linkage → id recomputation → sig recomputation; fails closed on the FIRST broken row with at_seq and count_checked.
outputs: {ok:true, count, tip, dialect} or {ok:false, error, at_seq, detail}
parts.gate: every id and sig re-derives; first failure wins
parts.failure_mode: any of the eight named codes, localized at at_seq

parts.name: five-field strictness
parts.essence: Exactly {seq, prev, body, id, sig}: missing fields and unknown fields both refuse — no client can add semantics the verifier does not check.
parts.gate: REQUIRED_FIELDS membership is exact in both directions

parts.name: seq/prev linkage checks
parts.essence: seq must equal row index+1 (covers replay of an old receipt) and prev must equal the previous row's id (the broken-hash-link case).
parts.gate: total order is contiguous and parent-bound

parts.name: validateAppend admission ladder
parts.essence: The write-side order: structure → body shape (body.kind, body.ts non-empty strings) → seq = tip+1 → prev = tip id → id recompute → sig recompute; first failure wins and returns isError:true with the named code.
parts.gate: nothing invalid is ever appended to disk
parts.failure_mode: E_BODY_INVALID | E_MISSING_FIELD | E_UNKNOWN_FIELD | E_SEQ_MISMATCH | E_PREV_MISMATCH | E_HASH_MISMATCH | E_BAD_SIGNATURE

parts.name: append-only write primitive
parts.essence: fs.appendFileSync of exactly one JSON line; there is no update verb and no delete verb anywhere in the server — mutation is not an operation it performs, and verify_chain catches edits done behind its back.
parts.gate: no code path rewrites or truncates the store (demo seeding only fills an empty store)

parts.name: verifier-not-co-signer stance
parts.essence: No draft tool, no sign_receipt helper — signing key material never flows through the wire; the client constructs and signs, the server validates; the reference signer lives in examples/, outside the server.
parts.gate: the server never holds or transports client key material beyond its own HMAC secret

parts.name: stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 transport
parts.essence: Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 loop: parse errors → -32700, non-2.0/invalid requests → -32600, notifications (id absent) never reply; buffer-split line handling keeps partial reads honest.
parts.gate: a notification never produces a reply; an unparseable line still answers -32700

parts.name: MCP handshake + tool surface
parts.essence: initialize negotiates the protocol version (echoes any 20xx- requested version, else 2024-11-05), advertises capabilities {tools:{listChanged:false}} + serverInfo; tools/list returns exactly the three tools with input schemas; unknown method → -32601, unknown tool name → -32602.
outputs: capabilities + serverInfo | tool descriptors | tool results
parts.gate: the wire surface is exactly three tools; nothing else is callable
parts.failure_mode: -32601 method not found | -32602 invalid params/unknown tool

parts.name: read_receipts recall with cursor
parts.essence: Returns receipts with seq > since_seq capped at limit∈[1,1000]; bad args refuse with E_BAD_ARGS; corrupted_lines ride along in the payload when present — recall stays honest about its own substrate.
parts.gate: since_seq must be a non-negative integer; limit in [1,1000]

parts.name: demo seeding that never deletes
parts.essence: --demo seeds 5 fleet-real receipts (genesis, engine.run.sealed, lesson.minted, organ.boot.verified, scout.report.landed) ONLY into an empty/missing store, and refuses to seed a corrupt store — the convenience path cannot become an eraser.
outputs: seeded store + stderr notice with tip
parts.gate: seed only if receipts.length === 0 and no corrupted lines

parts.name: dev-secret loud warning
parts.essence: When the built-in fallback HMAC secret is in use the server warns on stderr (unless --quiet-notice) — an honest residual: HMAC shared-secret signing means any writer holds full signing power.

cells.expr: read store.jsonl each call; JSON.parse per line; collect corrupted_lines
re-derive every row from genesis; first failure wins with named code at at_seq
JSON.parse or -32700; notifications silent; dispatch by method
filter seq>since_seq, slice limit, surface corrupted_lines
validate then append; return {ok,seq,id,tip,dialect} or isError named code
seed 5 fleet receipts only into an empty, uncorrupted store

layer_logic.0: Canonical JSON + SHA-256 + HMAC-SHA256: a receipt is five fields whose id binds seq:prev:body and whose sig binds the id — the irreducible representation of a fleet memory line.
layer_logic.1: loadStore + verifyChain transform raw file bytes into a verified total order from genesis, with no cache and no silent skips — the mechanism is re-derivation, every time.
layer_logic.2: Policy = admission ladder: nothing invalid is ever written; no update/delete verbs exist; the server verifies and never co-signs; the shared-secret residual is stated, not hidden.
layer_logic.3: Interface = stdio newline JSON-RPC 2.0 speaking MCP: initialize/ping/tools.list/tools.call, exactly three tools, protocol error codes for everything malformed.
layer_logic.4: Evidence = verify_chain's named codes at named at_seq (the tamper trio proven in the wire suite), corrupted_lines on recall, tip comparison to detect forks, and a stderr warning whenever the dev secret is trusted.
